images.title: More than the multiplier
images.purpose: Show that the HCF of 14 × 6 and 14 × 9 is 14 times the shared 3 of 6 and 9, which is 42, not just 14.
images.composition: Two rows of factor blocks on the left half, one under the other, and a single result line on the right, with wide white space between.
exact_structure: Row 1: the label 84 = then exactly 3 blocks side by side: a wide teal #0072B2 block 14, a small reddish purple #CC79A7 block 3, a small amber #E69F00 block 2.
Row 2: the label 126 = then exactly 3 blocks side by side: a wide teal #0072B2 block 14, a small reddish purple #CC79A7 block 3, a small amber #E69F00 block 3.

The blocks of both rows start at the same x position, so the two teal 14 blocks, the two reddish purple 3 blocks and the two amber blocks are vertically aligned; the two reddish purple 3 blocks are joined by one thin grey #6B7280 vertical line.
To the right, one bold line: HCF = 14 × 3 = 42.
rejection: blocks whose product does not equal the number at the start of their row (84 = 14 × 2 × 3, 126 = 14 × 3 × 3)
more or fewer than 3 blocks in either row, or more or fewer than 2 reddish purple blocks
any of the numbers 90, 48, 180, 380, 65 or 192 appearing
images.takeaway: The HCF of two multiples of the same number can be bigger than that number when the other factors share something.
images.description: 84 shown as blocks 14, 3, 2 and 126 as blocks 14, 3, 3, with the shared 3 linked, and HCF = 14 × 3 = 42.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on multiples of the same number.
images.teaching_notes: Look past the shared 14 to the small blocks: 6 and 9 share a 3, so it joins the HCF.

image_decisions.why: Factor blocks show at once the common multiplier and the extra shared factor that makes the HCF larger.
